objective.statement: Resolve the confirmed dotfiles review findings while preserving unrelated operator edits.
objective.measure: Focused regressions and repo check pass; no tracked plaintext Exa credential remains.

need.statement: The review found an exposed Exa credential, a failing model contract, unsafe cleanup inputs, an incomplete dirty-tree build gate, narrow shell lint scope, and a prompt timeout.
need.baseline: repo check fails on Codex Luna routing; review reproductions identify the remaining gaps.
need.consequence_of_no_action: Credentials remain exposed and safety/verification gaps continue.

assumptions.statement: The existing Exa credential is the intended value to preserve while moving it to SOPS.
assumptions.falsifier: The operator supplies a replacement or revocation instruction before activation.

purpose: Resolve the confirmed dotfiles review findings while preserving unrelated operator edits.
consumer: Dotfiles operators, Home Manager activation, OpenCode, Codex, and repository gates.
contract: Exa authentication is encrypted in SOPS and injected at runtime; Luna roles and tests agree on gpt-6.1-luna; dirty activation changes trigger the Nix build gate; cleanup scripts reject unsafe inputs and agent ancestry is narrow; shell checks cover managed shell entrypoints; Starship no longer times out the reported rustc probe.
failure_boundary: Unrelated existing worktree edits remain untouched; invalid secrets or unsafe cleanup inputs fail closed; a failed verification blocks completion.

evidence.description: Focused tests plus repo check and diff inspection.

executable_check.description: A focused regression or repo check still fails, or plaintext Exa credentials remain.

invariants: SOPS remains the source of truth for provider credentials
Repository VCS changes use the declared facade

assumptions.statement: OpenCode supports the existing {env:NAME} interpolation used by its GitHub MCP header.
assumptions.falsifier: The focused config test or live OpenCode config parser rejects the placeholder.
